findings.title: Team permission requires being both admin and owner
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, so a team admin who is not the owner, or an owner who is not also returned as an admin, fails the check. Unless the caller is also the organizer or an attendee, legitimate team admins/owners are incorrectly rejected with FORBIDDEN. The two role checks should be combined with OR.

findings.title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking
findings.body: The authorization accepts anyone whose email appears in booking.attendees. An invited guest can therefore call this mutation directly to add unlimited arbitrary people to the organizer's booking, causing database attendees, calendar updates, and invitation emails to be created in the organizer's name. The new UI is on the organizer's bookings page, so attendee access is an unnecessary privilege expansion; only the organizer and authorized team admins/owners should be able to modify the guest list.

findings.title: Calendar is updated with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: EventManager is constructed from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). When the caller is a team admin/owner or another authorized user who is not the booking organizer, the calendar event is updated using the caller's credentials (or fails to find the organizer's calendar), even though the handler loads booking.user with credentials/destinationCalendar. The guests are already persisted before this step, so the database and the organizer's calendar can diverge.

findings.title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
findings.body: The handler checks authorization but never checks booking.status or booking.endTime before creating attendees, calling updateCalendarAttendees, and sending scheduled/add-guests emails. A cancelled, rejected, or already-finished booking can therefore gain new attendees and trigger fresh calendar invitations and emails as if it were still an upcoming confirmed event. The server should reject non-confirmed or past bookings, not only rely on which actions the list UI happens to render.

findings.title: Guest list has no uniqueness or size limit on the server
findings.body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema only requires each entry to be an email string. Direct API callers can submit duplicate addresses, duplicates differing only by case, or an arbitrarily large array; the client-side uniqueness refine in AddGuestsDialog does not protect the API. The handler's duplicate and blacklist checks are also case-sensitive for the submitted guest (the blacklist is lowercased, the guest is not), so createMany can insert duplicate attendees and the mutation can be used to fan out unbounded calendar updates and emails.

findings.title: Emails are classified using the unfiltered guest list
findings.body: The handler filters submissions into uniqueGuests (removing people already on the booking and blacklisted addresses) and persists only those, but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original list. In email-manager, any attendee whose email is in that list is sent AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, so an existing attendee who was resubmitted receives a fresh scheduled/invitation email rather than the guests-added notification. Pass uniqueGuests so email selection matches the attendees actually added.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore disabled standard email settings
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails always sends organizer, team-member, and attendee emails and accepts no eventTypeMetadata, unlike the neighboring location-change/scheduled flows which honor metadata.disableStandardEmails for hosts and attendees. The addGuests handler also does not pass booking.eventType.metadata. Event types that have disabled standard emails will still emit this new set of emails.
